steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
steps.detail: In the Developer portal Build section, select Connections and create a new connection. Choose Any workspace installation scope so other customer organizations can install it. Enter the connection name, development workspace, and redirect URIs, and select the read content capability. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation.
steps.doneWhen: A public OAuth integration exists with a client ID, client secret, authorization URL in the Configuration tab, a redirect URI, and read content capability enabled.

steps.title: Store OAuth client credentials securely
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab to copy the OAuth client ID, client secret and authorization URL. Store them in environment variables or a secret manager, never in source code or version control.
steps.doneWhen: CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET and the authorization URL are available to the server from environment configuration.

evidence.quote: After creating an OAuth integration in the Developer portal , access the connection’s secrets in the Configuration tab. Similarly to the internal connections, these values should be protected and should
never be included in source code or version control.

steps.title: Customer authorizes the app and shares pages in the page picker
steps.detail: Direct the customer to the authorization URL from the Configuration tab. The consent prompt describes read capabilities. The customer selects pages in the page picker and clicks Allow access, which redirects to the redirect URI with a code. This is a manual consent step; no code is generated by the agent.
steps.doneWhen: The customer completes Allow access and the browser lands on the redirect URI with a code query parameter, and the selected pages are shared.

evidence.quote: Once the authorization URL is visited, the user will be shown a prompt that varies depending on whether or not the connection comes with a Notion template option.

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Send the code from the redirect to the token endpoint with HTTP Basic authentication using CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET and a JSON body with grant_type authorization_code, code and redirect_uri. Store the returned access_token, refresh_token and bot_id per customer. This is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id, stored against that customer.

steps.title: Read the title and markdown content of a shared page
steps.detail: Using the customer's access token, retrieve a shared page to read its title from the properties object, then retrieve its markdown content. Expected success is HTTP 200 with the title in properties.title and content in the markdown field. Boundary check: request a page the customer did not share and expect 404, confirming access is limited to shared pages.
steps.doneWhen: The title and markdown content of a shared page are returned with 200, and an unshared page returns 404.
